purpose: Test the most direct repair of the one-row-pair Cauchy-Binet selector: give each Boolean value an r-row bundle so one global variable choice can feed r clause occurrences, and ask the selector matrix to admit exactly the all-0 bundle or all-1 bundle but no mixed bundle.

theorem.name: ORDINARY_CAUCHY_BINET_SELECTOR_CANNOT_ATOMICALLY_CHOOSE_BETWEEN_TWO_DISJOINT_MULTIROW_BUNDLES_V0_6
theorem.statement: Let K be any field and A be a rank-r matrix whose columns include two disjoint r-element sets B0 and B1. If det A[:,B0] != 0 and det A[:,B1] != 0, then for every e in B0 there exists f in B1 such that det A[:,(B0-{e}) union {f}] != 0. Hence for r>=2 no ordinary matrix selector can have B0 and B1 as the only nonzero r-column minors on B0 union B1.
proof: The supports of the nonzero rank-r minors of A are exactly the bases of the column matroid M(A).
B0 and B1 are bases because their determinants are nonzero.
Apply the matroid basis-exchange axiom: for every e in B0\B1 there exists f in B1\B0 such that (B0-{e}) union {f} is also a basis.
A set is a basis of M(A) exactly when the corresponding rank-r minor is nonzero.
Therefore at least one hybrid minor is nonzero for each e; the selector cannot permit exactly the two coherent bundles while zeroing all mixed bundles.
theorem.direct_linear_algebra_proof_shape: Because B0 is a basis, express every column of B1 in B0-coordinates. Since B1 is also a basis, the coordinate matrix is invertible. Every row of an invertible matrix has a nonzero entry; replacing the corresponding B0 column by that B1 column yields a nonzero hybrid determinant.

sat_fanout_consequence.killed_repair: Use Cauchy-Binet with an ordinary selector matrix A to choose r occurrence rows for x_i=0 or r occurrence rows for x_i=1 atomically, with every mixed choice killed by zero selector minor.
sat_fanout_consequence.reason: For a variable appearing in r>=2 coupled clause locations, both coherent bundles must survive, but basis exchange forces hybrid selections that represent inconsistent local copies.
sat_fanout_consequence.relation_to_v0_3_v0_4: v0.3 showed exact Boolean assignment summation when one row is selected from each pair; v0.4 killed universal SAT support in that local model. v0.6 shows that the simplest multirow fanout repair cannot be implemented merely by replacing each row choice with an atomic block choice inside an ordinary Cauchy-Binet selector.

ruled_out: zero-by-support atomic r-row bundle selection with ordinary matrix minors
direct determinant fanout that relies solely on vanishing all hybrid selector minors
fixed mandatory padding followed by the same atomic block-selector idea
not_ruled_out: constructions where hybrid subsets survive but cancel globally
Pfaffian or matchgate constructions with additional algebraic structure

next_constructive_target.name: E8_GLOBAL_HYBRID_CANCELLATION_OR_COLORED_DETERMINANT_V0_7
next_constructive_target.directive: Stop trying to enforce fanout by zeroing every inconsistent mixed selector subset. Permit hybrids and seek a polynomial-size global sign/color involution that cancels all inconsistent hybrids while leaving at least one nonzero contribution exactly when SAT.
success_obligations: proof that every inconsistent hybrid contribution is paired/cancelled
proof that satisfying coherent contributions do not all cancel
